Heteroskedasticity    Definition and consequences

Heteroskedasticity



Definition:

     Heteroskedasticity refers to a condition in which the variance of the random
      error term u in a regression model varies widely.

                     V ar(ui|xi) = σ2h(xi) ̸= σ2

Consequences remain the same:

    OLS estimators are still unbiased and consistent.
     Interpretation of R2 does not change.

Consequences that change significantly:
    Formula for calculating V ar(ˆβj) is invalid.
    The t-test and F-test are invalid.

    OLS estimators may not be the most efficient estimators.

Heteroskedasticity    Heteroskedasticity-robust inference

Heteroskedasticity-robust standard error


Motivation:

      Practically, we do not know the real form of heteroskedasticity.

     Heteroskedasticity-robust inference helps calculate a valid estimator for
    V ar(ˆβj) in large samples.

Testing for Heteroskedasticity   Breusch-Pagan test

Breusch-Pagan test





Test for the null hypothesis with multiple restrictions:

                   H0 : δ1 = δ2 = · · · = δk = 0

where δ1, δ2, · · · , δk are the coefficients from the regression model:

                               ˆu2i = δ0 + δ1x1i + · · · + δkxki + ϵi

Rejection rule:
              R2ˆu2/k   F =               > cα(k, n −k −1).          (1−R2                ˆu2)/(n−k−1)
      Fail to reject does not necessarily mean accepting homoskedasticity.

Testing for Heteroskedasticity   White test

White test


Presume that there are 3 independent variables: x1, x2, x3.


Test for the null hypothesis with multiple restrictions:

                   H0 : δ1 = δ2 = · · · = δ9 = 0

where δ1, δ2, · · · , δk are the coefficients from the regression model:

                 ˆu2i = δ0 + δ1x1i + δ2x2i + δ3x3i + δ4x21i + δ5x22i + δ6x23i

                    +δ7x1ix2i + δ8x1ix3i + δ9x2ix3i + ϵi

Comments for white test:

      F-statistic is used to carry out the statistical inference.

     Detect more deviations from homoskedasticity than BP test.
   A large number (2k + C2k) of parameters are needed to be estimated.

Testing for Heteroskedasticity   White test: an alternative expression

White test: an alternative expression




Presume that there are k independent variables: x1, x2, · · · , xk:

                          yi = β0 + β1x1i + · · · + βkxki + ui



Test for the null hypothesis with multiple restrictions:

                      H0 : δ1 = δ2 = 0

where δ1, δ2 are the coefficients from the regression model:

                                    ˆu2i = δ0 + δ1ˆyi + δ2ˆy2i + ϵi

Weighted Least Squares   The heteroskedasticity is known up to a multiplicative constant

Known up to a multiplicative constant


Assume that we know the real form of the heteroskedasticity:

                       V ar(ui|xi) = σ2hi

where hi > 0, hi is the function of xi.


Let the original model:

                          yi = β0 + β1x1i + · · · + βkxki + ui
be divided by √hi, then we have:

                    yi       1        x1i            xki     ui
             √hi = β0 √hi + β1 √hi + · · · + βk √hi + √hi

or
                    y∗i = β0x∗0i + β1x∗1i + · · · + βkx∗ki + u∗i

Weighted Least Squares   Weighted least squares

Weighted least squares



The transformed model is solved by this minimization:

                                                  1
                      minβ0,··· ,βkΣni=1wi(ˆui)2, where wi =
                                                          hi

This method is called the weighted least squares, in which each squared residual
in the minimization process is weighted.


Comments for WLS:
    V ar(u∗i |xi) = σ2, t-test and F-test are valid in large samples.
    The weighted least squares estimators are BLUEs under MLR.1-MLR.4.

   WLS is a special case of the generalized least squares (GLS).

       If the form of heteroskedasticity is unknown, we apply feasible GLS (FGLS),
    which uses an estimated weight.

Stata Commands

Syntax


After estimating a linear model by using OLS, we can test for heteroskedasticity.


BP-test:

                                    estat hettest

White test:

                                  estat imtest,white

 If heteroskedasticity is perceived, we can let the Stata show the
heteroskedasticity-robust error:

                                 reg y x1 x2 x3,r

or use weighted least squares:

                            reg y x1 x2 x3 [aw=1/hi]
